project.title: The Sky Mender / 天幕修补师

shots.beat: The repair cable catches as the sky fissure widens.

planned.identity: One human sky-repair worker with a stable silhouette and dark brass climbing harness.
planned.wardrobe_props: Heavy red oilcloth cape with one triangular lower edge; compact amber repair torch in the right hand; steel safety cable anchored lower-left.
planned.space_direction: Worker stays left of the vertical sky fissure and moves screen-right on the tower exterior.
planned.motion: Worker ends swinging screen-right as the safety cable first becomes taut.
planned.light_material: Cold storm daylight from upper camera-left; amber fissure bounce on wet brass and oilcloth.
planned.story_beat: The repair attempt begins, but the fissure widens and pulls the worker off the tower rib.

grammar.narrative_moment: End on the instant the safety cable catches the falling worker, before recovery.
grammar.camera_movement: Measured wide observation from a neighboring gantry, then a lateral track at subject speed without crossing the tower axis.
grammar.light_color: Cold source-bound storm daylight from upper camera-left with a narrow amber reflection from the fissure.
grammar.space_composition: Tower ribs provide fixed depth; worker remains left of the fissure and travels screen-right toward open cloud space.
grammar.material_physics: Wet brass and oilcloth carry weight; the cable goes taut before body direction changes; the cape trails downwind.

prompt.text: A lone sky-repair worker climbs the exterior maintenance ribs of an immense weathered tower above a storm cloud ocean. The worker has a stable human silhouette, a dark brass climbing harness, a heavy red oilcloth cape with one triangular lower edge, and a compact amber repair torch held in the right hand. A narrow luminous fissure runs vertically through the cloud ceiling to the worker's right. In one continuous five-second shot, begin with a measured wide view from a physically plausible neighboring gantry, then track laterally at the worker's speed as the worker clips a steel safety cable to the tower and reaches the torch toward the fissure. Cold storm daylight comes from upper camera-left; the amber fissure adds a restrained warm reflection to wet brass and cloth. The fissure suddenly widens, a pressure gust tears the worker's boots from the rib, and the shot ends before recovery: the worker is swinging screen-right, the cable has just snapped taut from the lower-left anchor, the cape is pulled downwind, and the torch remains visible in the right hand. Preserve tower geography and screen direction. Real weight, wet surfaces, cable tension, and wind-driven cloth; no cuts, no teleporting camera, no heroic pose, no decorative smoke, no text, no logo.
